candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — client rights, advocacy, abuse/neglect reporting and legal responsibilities
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — reporting suspected abuse in long-term care
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to suspected resident abuse in a federally certified nursing facility by protecting the resident and initiating required reporting without delaying for independent proof.

options.A: Report the allegation immediately through the facility's required process and to the officials specified by federal and applicable state requirements rather than waiting to prove that abuse occurred
options.B: Wait until the nurse personally completes a full investigation and obtains definitive proof before any report is made
options.C: Document the observation only in the resident's record and take no further reporting action
options.D: Confront the staff member privately and keep the incident within the unit unless the resident later develops an injury

candidate.rationale: Federal long-term-care requirements at 42 CFR 483.12 require facilities to protect residents from abuse and to ensure alleged violations involving abuse, neglect, exploitation, mistreatment, or misappropriation are reported promptly to required facility and governmental officials. Reporting is triggered by an allegation; staff should not delay required reporting while attempting to prove the case independently. The facility must also investigate and protect the resident while the allegation is addressed.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Federally certified nursing facilities must promptly report allegations of abuse and protect residents; reporting cannot be postponed until staff independently prove the allegation.
candidate.source_document_title: 42 CFR Part 483, Subpart B — Requirements for Long Term Care Facilities; §483.12 Freedom from abuse, neglect, and exploitation
candidate.source_locator: 42 CFR §483.12(c): facility must ensure alleged violations are reported immediately to the administrator and required officials; reporting deadlines depend on whether abuse/serious bodily injury is involved; facility must investigate and prevent further potential abuse
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services / Code of Federal Regulations
candidate.stem: A nurse in a Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing facility observes another staff member strike a resident. The resident is now safe and does not appear to have serious bodily injury. Which action is most appropriate?
